(i) the plasma screening effect is not sufficient to explain the suppression of charmonium in a quark-gluon plasma, (ii) the plasma Hamiltonian approach provides the necessary extension of the plasma screening model and (iii) the plasma screening model can be applied to calculate quarkonium dissociative rates in a quark gluon plasma

the in-medium modification (suppresion, shift, broadening) of heavy quarkonium states can be described by the same effective plasma Hamiltonian as the modification of the light meson spectrum, that this effective plasma Hamiltonian is a nonperturbative result of the underlying strong interactions in the medium, and that the resulting in-medium modification of heavy quark states is governed by the same physical mechanisms that are also relevant for the light hadronic spectrum.

the plasma Hamiltonian is the main tool to study quarkonium properties in the quark-gluon plasma and that it contains all the physics of the Mott dissociation effect as well as the physics of the quark-guon plasma dissociation effect.

we have developed a consistent framework for the calculation of the spectral functions of heavy quarkonium states in a medium.

we have provided a theoretical framework to calculate in-medium modifications of heavy quarkonium states, which can be applied in the case of a strongly correlated quark-gluon plasma, but also for a hot and dense hadronic matter.

the plasma Hamiltonian approach is a useful tool to describe the in-medium properties of heavy quarkonium states.
